question: What is the main goal of offering family planning right after an abortion?

options.A: To delay physical healing after pregnancy loss
options.B: To check for lower abdominal infections
options.C: To stop pregnancy from ever happening again
options.D: To help prevent rapid, unplanned repeat pregnancies

explanation: Offering contraception right away helps patients protect their bodies and avoid another unplanned pregnancy before they feel ready. You've got this!

question: Why is it so important to talk about family planning right after an abortion?

options.A: Patients lose natural immunity without hormonal birth control
options.B: Hormonal pills speed up physical recovery from a miscarriage
options.C: Fertility returns very quickly after an abortion procedure
options.D: Patients are required by law to start birth control immediately

explanation: Ovulation can happen as early as two weeks after an abortion! That means a patient can get pregnant again before their next period even arrives.

question: How soon can a patient start ovulating again after an abortion?

options.A: Only after three normal monthly cycles

explanation: The ovaries can release an egg just two weeks post-abortion, even before bleeding stops. Good to keep in mind for patient education!

question: A patient asks if she can get pregnant before her first period returns after an abortion. What should you tell her?

options.A: No, menstruation must happen first to clear the path
options.B: No, the body is completely sterile for three months
options.C: Yes, because ovulation happens before the first period returns
options.D: Only if she had a surgical procedure instead of a medical one

explanation: Many patients are surprised by this! Ovulation happens first, meaning pregnancy is possible before that first post-abortion period shows up.

question: What is the main benefit of using a person-centred approach in post-abortion counseling?

options.A: It helps match birth control to the client's unique lifestyle and goals
options.B: It guarantees the patient will never feel any grief
options.C: It speeds up the clinic discharge paperwork
options.D: It forces the client to choose the strongest long-term method

explanation: Person-centred care is all about listening to what the patient wants. When they choose a method that fits their life, they are much happier using it!

question: Which attitude is most important for a nurse during post-abortion counseling?
explanation: Being warm, kind, and non-judgmental builds trust, making the patient feel safe to share their worries and ask questions.

question: Which type of birth control protects against both unplanned pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?
explanation: Condoms and other barrier methods act as a physical shield against both sperm and infections. Simple and effective!

question: A patient wants an IUD right after an uncomplicated surgical abortion. What is the standard clinical practice?

options.A: She must wait for two normal menstrual periods
options.B: It can be safely inserted right away if there is no sign of infection
options.C: IUDs are never recommended after pregnancy termination
options.D: She must wait six weeks for her uterus to shrink

explanation: As long as there's no infection or trauma, an IUD can be placed immediately after the procedure. Saves the patient an extra trip!

question: When is the best time to start a chosen birth control method after an abortion?

options.A: Only after the six-week follow-up visit
options.B: On the exact same day as the abortion procedure
options.C: After waiting for three complete menstrual cycles

explanation: Starting contraception on day one ensures the patient is protected before ovulation sneaks up on them.

question: What is the main risk of waiting until a six-week check-up to start birth control?

options.A: The patient may experience an unplanned pregnancy before the visit
options.B: The body will reject hormonal methods after six weeks
options.C: The patient's natural hormone levels will drop permanently
options.D: It becomes illegal to prescribe birth control then

explanation: Since ovulation can return in just two weeks, waiting six weeks leaves a huge window for another unintended pregnancy.

question: A patient refuses birth control pills because she heard they cause permanent infertility. How should you reply?

options.A: Ignore her concern and write the prescription anyway
options.B: Explain that fertility returns quickly once pills are stopped
options.C: Tell her infertility is the price for effective protection
options.D: Agree with her and suggest only natural calendar tracking

explanation: Clearing up this myth reassures the patient that her body will be ready to conceive in the future whenever she chooses.

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier stopping women from using post-abortion contraception?

options.B: Lack of transport to the clinic
options.D: High product costs at the pharmacy

explanation: High effectiveness is a great thing! Fear, cost, and travel issues are the real hurdles patients face.

question: A patient calls two days after an abortion saying she is soaking through three large pads every hour. What should you tell her?

options.A: Reassure her that heavy bleeding lasts a whole month
options.B: Tell her it is normal and to call back next week
options.C: Take extra birth control pills to slow down the flow
options.D: Come to the clinic or emergency department right away

explanation: Soaking more than two pads an hour for two hours is a major red flag for heavy bleeding. She needs medical attention urgently!

question: Why do we schedule a follow-up visit a few weeks after starting post-abortion family planning?

options.A: To run routine blood tests for hidden diseases
options.B: To close her medical file and discharge her forever
options.C: To force the patient to buy a more expensive brand
options.D: To check physical healing and see if her birth control method suits her

explanation: Follow-ups let us confirm she is healing nicely and make sure her birth control method is working comfortably for her lifestyle.
